quote: Send me an email or send a hard copy of how your company can help me with my,
stewart_read: This is a customer-stated alternative channel request, structurally similar to a protocol the rep should follow rather than argue — she is not objecting to solar, she is specifying HOW she wants to continue. The rep never routes to this alternative at any point in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have believed offering email/mail was against policy or unavailable, making this a knowledge gap rather than a refusal. But the rep never states any such constraint out loud — he simply reasserts he can help 'right now,' which is a redirection, not a stated policy limit.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly acknowledge and either honor or clearly explain why a customer's requested channel can't be used — silence on the request reads as dismissive.

quote: electric bill. Yeah. I can help you right now.
stewart_read: Rather than acknowledging what the customer just asked for, the rep asserts his own preferred channel ('right now') over hers. This is the first of three moments where the same unaddressed request recurs.
coaching_implication: This is the first entry in the recurring pattern flagged in multi_touch_patterns — replay it with the rep as the moment the call should have pivoted to 'I hear you, let's get this to you by email' instead of pressing forward.

quote: or send me a hard copy in the mail. You have my address. That's my mailing address.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly confirms Ion already has her mailing address on file, removing any logistical reason the rep might have had for not honoring the mail request. The rep does not engage with this at all — he pivots immediately to defending the need for phone questions ('everything we do is specific to homes').
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may not have access to mailing/emailing tools on this call and this is a genuine capability gap rather than a dismissal. But since he never states that constraint, the transcript only supports that he ignored a fully actionable request.
coaching_implication: Point out to the rep that she removed his only plausible excuse (no address on file) and he still didn't offer to send anything — this is the strongest evidence that the request was simply not registered as something to act on.

quote: Oh, so you haven't gotten enough information about me to to get to send you a quote?
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a sharp, logical challenge — she filled out a form, so why does he need more from her before sending anything? This is a moment where a flip ('exactly — that's why these three questions get you a real number instead of a generic one') could reframe the ask as being in her interest. The rep instead just repeats 'three other questions' again.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the call already lost and simply been trying to close it out efficiently, making this a deliberate wind-down rather than a missed flip. But the rep's own words ('That's fine... I literally just have, like, three other questions') show he is still trying to press forward, not disengaging.
coaching_implication: Show the rep this exact line as a textbook opening for a value-based reframe he walked past.

quote: I want to send you a quote because I already have quotes from two other companies.
stewart_read: Customer discloses she already has two competing quotes — real competitive intelligence that would help a closer. The rep does not ask which companies or what those quotes showed; he moves straight back to his own question count.
coaching_implication: Even in a call trending toward a hang-up, a 5-second 'oh who were those with?' costs nothing and banks competitive intel for the file.

quote: Sometimes it just it's a little it doesn't stick.
stewart_read: This line is halting and filler-heavy at a moment when the customer is already irritated about repeating information — the lack of a clean, confident answer compounds her frustration rather than defusing it.
coaching_implication: Coach crisper, more direct responses to redundancy pushback — a confident one-line reason for re-verification lands better than a stumbling half-sentence.

quote: I'm not required to answer your questions on the phone.
stewart_read: The call ends with no next step, no acknowledgment of what she actually asked for (email/mail), and no attempt at a final pivot — just 'I never said you were... goodbye.' There is no handshake, no confirmation of any future contact method, nothing owned by the rep.
alternative_hypothesis: Some calls are genuinely unrecoverable and ending cleanly is the right move. But even an unrecoverable call has a better close available — e.g., confirming he'll send the email she asked for — which the rep never offers even as an exit line.
coaching_implication: When a call is clearly ending, the last available move is to honor the customer's stated request as the final gesture — coach the rep to close with 'I'll get that email sent to you' rather than just goodbye.
